paper.title: VoiceMem: Streaming Dual-Brain Memory for Real-Time Interaction

evidence.section: Full paper (arXiv HTML): Sec. 4.1 Stage III (construction); Sec. 5.3 (results)
evidence.paraphrase: ChatMem-Bench is a new human-curated benchmark of 316 questions drawn from roughly 53 hours of spoken dialogue, built for long-horizon evaluation of voice-assistant memory. It is audio-grounded: evaluated systems consume the spoken dialogue rather than a transcript.

Four ability dimensions with 14 fine-grained subcategories: Information (update tracking, temporal reasoning, synthesis, abstention), Persona (profile constraints, preference-aligned recommendation, implicit-need inference), Affective Attribution (emotion-target mapping, attachment-guided decisions, affect-aware phrasing), and Paralinguistics & Environment (background-sound recall, acoustic-scene inference, multi-user conversational memory, acoustic style adaptation).

The Paralinguistics & Environment dimension isolates memory that survives transcription loss: text-only memory systems score between 3.23 and 26.92 on the three acoustic categories while VoiceMem scores 45.16 to 53.84, making the benchmark a direct test of whether non-lexical acoustic evidence is retained across a long dialogue.

adjudication_notes: Recorded separately from the VoiceMem architecture record per counting_rules.md; the paper contributes both a memory architecture and a new benchmark.

The reported number of source dialogue turns was inconsistent across two retrievals of the same HTML (5,314 vs 15,314), so the turn count is deliberately omitted; the 316-question and ~53-hour figures were consistent.
Sec. 4.1 states the dialogues are human-curated from synthetic material, so the benchmark is partly synthetic rather than fully naturalistic.
